correctness.rationale: For five distinct complex plane points with exactly one collinear triple, the anticanonical class is nef and big of square 4. Adjunction and Cauchy–Schwarz give only five exceptional and seven ordinary pair-line (-1)-curves plus the triple-line (-2)-curve. Pairwise disjointness of selected (-1)-curves and a one-neighbor Schur bound for the (-2)-curve are necessary and sufficient for negative definiteness. The explicit F_m, G_m, H_2 formulas yield finite-support coefficients (1,12,46,72,43,4) and R-support coefficients (0,1,12,40,44,10). An independent exact rational enumeration of all 8192 principal submatrices and separate integer polynomial algebra matches both vectors and 285 total; the finite/infinite volume characterization follows directly from Bauer–Schmitz Theorem 1.4. No finite experiment substitutes for the geometric negative-curve proof.

value.rationale: The single A1 exceptional root is the first boundary stratum of quartic del Pezzo five-point geometry. The theorem gives every stable-base-locus support size in that stratum, quantifies the drop from the classical 393 smooth chambers to 285, and detects precisely 107 anticanonically unbounded chambers versus 178 finite ones. These are natural exact invariants not read off from 393 or the abstract volume criterion, and the rational combinatorial formulas isolate the geometric contribution of the (-2)-root.
